observation.visible_scene: A close-up, fixed view of a chrome espresso machine portafilter positioned above a small clear glass that sits on a transparent acrylic holder over a metal drip tray. A thin, continuous stream of brown coffee falls from the portafilter spout into the glass, which already contains a layered coffee (dark liquid below, lighter crema on top). A black portafilter handle projects to the right. The background is a bright, out-of-focus white surface with faint reflections of the machine.
visible_changes: The coffee stream remains continuous and roughly steady from the first to the last frame, with no visible start or stop of the pour within the excerpt.
The liquid level inside the glass rises slowly and gradually over the segment; comparing the first and last frames, the top of the coffee/crema column is slightly higher at the end.
The light-brown crema layer on the surface appears to thicken and expand upward as the pour continues, while the darker coffee beneath stays relatively constant in height.

The portafilter, its black handle, the glass, the acrylic stand, and the background reflections remain in fixed positions throughout, indicating no camera movement and no object translation within the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: When the extraction began and when it will end are outside this segment; the glass is already partially filled at t=0 and still being filled at t=1.6s.
The final fill level, total volume extracted, and any post-pour actions (removing the glass, stopping the machine) are not shown.
The cause of the crema's texture change (e.g., pressure, grind) is not visible.
uncertain_details: The exact rate of level rise is small and hard to quantify frame-to-frame; only a modest net increase is supported.
Minor apparent thickness/shape variations in the falling stream may be image noise or slight flow fluctuation rather than deliberate change.
Whether there is any sub-pixel camera drift is indeterminate given the static background.
